text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- Chamber of Labour demands a road-pricing system for trucks on Austria's motorways must go ahead as planned. Otherwise it forecasts costs of 300 million schillings.
- A radical reform of Austria's energy industry could make prices tumble, energy agency says.
- Thomas Sykora is celebrated as the first Austrian ever to have won the Slalom World Cup title by coming ninth in the season's last run in Vail, USA. He won five runs this winter. DIE PRESSE
- Austria's high court has ruled that low rents for shops can only be raised slowly.
- On Wednesday Parliament will change the country's working laws to make ten-hour-workdays and four-day-weeks possible.
- Car insurance prices fall further as insurers go on selling special premiums to good drivers.
- Creditanstalt's chief executive Guido Schmidt-Chiari criticised Die Erste savings bank's role in the privatisation of Creditanstalt. He also announced his retirement.
- Bankrupt constructor Maculan Holding plans to restart business and relist the company.
- Austria's Volksbanken sector plans to intensify cooperation but does not want to merge.
- Catholic groups, conservatives and greens protest against the softening of a Sunday ban on working.
- Austria still has to wait seven months to join the European Union's Schengen agreement as German protests against the country's membership grow.
- Bank Austria is selling off parts of its industrial interests after taking over Creditanstalt, like Polish coal miner Polkarbon.
- Chamber of Economy wants to get farmers to agree to a reform of trade regulations.
